concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of planning as deciding in advance what to do and how to do it.
Explain that planning covers both ends (objectives) and means (courses of action) within a time frame.
Describe how planning provides direction, reduces uncertainty and waste, promotes innovation and aids decision making.
Explain why planning establishes the standards needed for controlling.
Explain that planning is purposeful and is the primary function of management.
Explain that planning is pervasive across levels and departments and is a continuous process.
Explain that planning is futuristic, involves decision making and is a mental exercise.
Explain how rigidity and a dynamic environment limit the usefulness of plans.
Explain how planning may reduce creativity, involve huge costs and consume time.
Explain why planning does not guarantee success.
Describe setting objectives and developing premises as the first steps of planning.
Distinguish identifying, evaluating and selecting alternative courses of action.
Describe implementing the plan and follow-up action.

topics.title: Single-use and standing plans
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Plans: Single-use and standing plans

concepts.learning_objective: Identify single-use plans as plans for one-time, non-recurring situations.
Identify standing plans as plans for recurring activities, including policies, procedures, methods and rules.

topics.title: Objectives, strategy, policy, procedure, method, rule, programme and budget
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Plans: Objectives to Budget

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish objectives as desired end results from strategy as a comprehensive long-term plan.
Distinguish policies, procedures, methods and rules as guides to action.
Explain programmes as detailed project statements and budgets as numerical plans that also aid control.
